accepts.because: a digest run demanded NOW, outside the timer: the same body the schedule emits -- one `tool_call` turn whose text is the JSON arguments carrying the URL. `chat_id` must be promoted to context by the caller (a string, as the timer's own header is), because the formatter recasts it into the delivery header and cannot invent one

a read of the last digests (GH #976, the residents' road of GH #965): hop `op` = `last`, `op_id` mirrored. Answered by exactly one `answer` `{ok, op, digests: [{id, at, when, title, items, lead, audience_set}]}`, newest first, holding only the digests whose round covers the round of the read (`context.audience_set`, the builder's word) -- or `{ok: false, error: {code: unknown_op | no_round | store_error}}`. A read without a round reads no row

emits.because: the formatted digest of a run that was demanded from outside, handed back to whoever demanded it instead of being pushed into this bot's own chat. A scheduled run goes to the notifier and never reaches this lane
the one answer to an `in_read`, with the asker's context, so the edge that asked can take it back; `op` and `op_id` mirrored, every digest with the round it was made for

a failure of `./access`, the broker that hands this template's cells their credentials sealed (GH #801): a refused or failed credential round. Which cell inside produced it is not the caller's business; a parent that drains nothing loses every refusal

edges.condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'ack' && has(hop.operation) && hop.operation == 'vault.deliver' && has(hop.grant_id) && hop.grant_id == 'grant:telegram-bot@template-daily-digest/notifier'

description.purpose: Composes timer, web_fetch, formatter and Telegram proxy into a linear scheduled push pipeline.
description.use_when: Daily one-URL digest to one chat, or a run demanded from outside on lane in_digest. Non-2xx fetches have no edge -- they dead-letter (wire a failure branch if you need alerting).
description.not_in_scope: No retries, no aggregation, no summarization.
examples: clock -> fetcher -> format -> notifier. chat_id travels: timer emit_headers (string) -> context on edge 1 -> recast to number by format -> context on edge 3. A run demanded at the hive path on lane in_digest enters at the fetcher with context.digest_origin 'parent' and its formatted digest leaves at the hive path on lane digest instead of going to the notifier; the caller brings context.chat_id itself.
